body:
Don Hargraves (hunza1@vixa.voyager.net) wrote:
:    The unibomber makes a case for two types of technology: the type that
: anyone can learn and master (glass staining and simple metallurgy) and
: technologies which need organization and by this nature demean the
: individual (automobiles, computers)
:    The criterion is not whether their use harms the user; as he notes
: himself each of these technologies by themselves looks good and is
: useful.  However, their final outcome is damaging in that they make the
: individual dependant on their use...those without cars are forced to
: subsistance living (if not utter poverty) by the chain effects of mass
: automobile ownership, computers make for a society unable to operate
: without them and which must fit itself within its limitations.

202.  It would be hopeless for revolutionaries to try to attack the
system without using SOME modern technology.  If nothing else they must
use the communications media to spread their message.  But they should
use modern technology for only ONE purpose: to attack the technological
system.

Paraphrased: Communication is necessary for revolutionaries to do their
work well, but they should not become reliant on the technology because
then they will need the system.  

Phone communications are something that might not have to be destroyed, 
but the computer is simply abused too frequently by corporations and
governments and while it could theoretically be restricted to only
communication use, it would be abused my members of the system at
first opportunity.

Debate in this group has degenerated in large part because those attempting
to attack FC have used the tired media arguments that are based on
misunderstandings and oversimplifications.  There's everything from
"he wasn't a productive citizen slave" to "I don't agree with the Manifesto
so it's wrong" to "All laws must be obeyed and killing is never justified
unless the law says it is."

Since the people who dislike FC use the same arguments, I think the
best possible response would be to thoroughly cover an explanation of
these repetitious topics.  Then when they try to argue, we can direct
them to the FAQ, though they probably won't understand that what the
guy on the 6 o'clock news said could be wrong.

Shall we start a list of topics so we can cut out the noise here?  Those
who are posting factual information on the UNABOM suspect's case and
general revolutionary information are the only ones holding this group
together.  Let's see if we can keep up the quality here.

-Ric
